e-5182.knowledge_point: Applying a Laplace Expansion Across a Row
e-5182.problem:
Using a cofactor expansion along the $4$th row, write the following determinant as a combination of $3 \times 3$ determinants:

$$
\begin{aligned}10 & 2 & -2 & -1 \\ 1 & -2 & 7 & 9 \\ -2 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ -6 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}
$$
e-5182.worked_solution:
Using a Laplace expansion along the $4$th row, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}10 & 2 & -2 & -1 \\ 1 & -2 & 7 & 9 \\ -2 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ -6 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}| & =(-6)\cdot {C}_{41}+0\cdot {C}_{42}+0\cdot {C}_{43}+1\cdot {C}_{44} \\  & =(-6)\cdot (-1)^{4+1}\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & -1 \\ -2 & 7 & 9 \\ 1 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}|+1\cdot (-1)^{4+4}\cdot |\begin{aligned}10 & 2 & -2 \\ 1 & -2 & 7 \\ -2 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =6\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & -1 \\ -2 & 7 & 9 \\ 1 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}|+|\begin{aligned}10 & 2 & -2 \\ 1 & -2 & 7 \\ -2 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}10 & 2 & -2 & -1 \\ 1 & -2 & 7 & 9 \\ -2 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ -6 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}
$$

e-4418.knowledge_point: Calculating a Determinant Using a Laplace Expansion Across a Row
e-4418.worked_solution:
The $4$th row of the matrix contains three zeros, more than any other row. So using a Laplace expansion along the $4$th row, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 & 2 \\ 0 & -2 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}| & =0\cdot {C}_{41}+0\cdot {C}_{42}+0\cdot {C}_{43}+(-1)\cdot {C}_{44} \\  & =(-1)\cdot (-1)^{4+4}\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 \\ 0 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =-|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 \\ 0 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, computing the $3 \times 3$ determinant by applying a Laplace expansion along the $1$st row, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 \\ 0 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}| & =1\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & -4 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}|-(-1)\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & -4 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}|+0\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}1 & -4 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}|+|\begin{aligned}0 & -4 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =(3-8)+(0-0) \\  & =-5\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 & 2 \\ 0 & -2 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}
$$

e-4419.knowledge_point: Calculating a Determinant Using a Laplace Expansion Across a Column
e-4419.problem:
Using a cofactor expansion along the $2$nd column, write the following determinant as a combination of $3 \times 3$ determinants:

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -3 & -2 \\ 2 & 3 & -1 & 5 \\ 1 & 0 & 8 & 9 \\ 2 & 0 & 3 & -1\end{aligned}
$$
e-4419.worked_solution:
Using a Laplace expansion along the $2$nd column, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -3 & -2 \\ 2 & 3 & -1 & 5 \\ 1 & 0 & 8 & 9 \\ 2 & 0 & 3 & -1\end{aligned}| & =0\cdot {C}_{12}+3\cdot {C}_{22}+0\cdot {C}_{32}+0\cdot {C}_{42} \\  & =3\cdot (-1)^{2+2}\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -2 \\ 1 & 8 & 9 \\ 2 & 3 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =3\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -2 \\ 1 & 8 & 9 \\ 2 & 3 & -1\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -3 & -2 \\ 2 & 3 & -1 & 5 \\ 1 & 0 & 8 & 9 \\ 2 & 0 & 3 & -1\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
The $2$nd row of the matrix contains two zeros, more than any other row. So, using a Laplace expansion along the $2$nd row, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}-7 & -1 & 5 & 8 \\ 3 & -6 & 0 & 0 \\ 4 & -3 & 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 3 & -5 & -7\end{aligned}| & =3\cdot {C}_{21}+(-6)\cdot {C}_{22}+0\cdot {C}_{23}+0\cdot {C}_{24} \\  & =3\cdot (-1)^{2+1}|\begin{aligned}-1 & 5 & 8 \\ -3 & 2 & -1 \\ 3 & -5 & -7\end{aligned}|+(-6)\cdot (-1)^{2+2}\cdot |\begin{aligned}-7 & 5 & 8 \\ 4 & 2 & -1 \\ 1 & -5 & -7\end{aligned}| \\  & =-3\cdot |\begin{aligned}-1 & 5 & 8 \\ -3 & 2 & -1 \\ 3 & -5 & -7\end{aligned}|-6\cdot |\begin{aligned}-7 & 5 & 8 \\ 4 & 2 & -1 \\ 1 & -5 & -7\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

content.worked_solution:
The $2$nd row of the matrix contains two zeros, more than any other row. So, using a Laplace expansion along the $2$nd row, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}-7 & -1 & 5 & 8 \\ 3 & -6 & 0 & 0 \\ 4 & -3 & 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 3 & -5 & -7\end{aligned}| & =3\cdot {C}_{21}+(-6)\cdot {C}_{22}+0\cdot {C}_{23}+0\cdot {C}_{24} \\  & =3\cdot (-1)^{2+1}|\begin{aligned}-1 & 5 & 8 \\ -3 & 2 & -1 \\ 3 & -5 & -7\end{aligned}|+(-6)\cdot (-1)^{2+2}\cdot |\begin{aligned}-7 & 5 & 8 \\ 4 & 2 & -1 \\ 1 & -5 & -7\end{aligned}| \\  & =-3\cdot |\begin{aligned}-1 & 5 & 8 \\ -3 & 2 & -1 \\ 3 & -5 & -7\end{aligned}|-6\cdot |\begin{aligned}-7 & 5 & 8 \\ 4 & 2 & -1 \\ 1 & -5 & -7\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Expand along the third row, whose only nonzero entry is 2 in column 4. Its cofactor sign is (-1)^{3+4}=-1, so the determinant equals -2 times the minor obtained by deleting row 3 and column 4. Thus option c is correct.

after.name: Question 2
after.worked_solution:
The $3$rd row of the matrix contains three zeros, more than any other row. So using a Laplace expansion along the $3$rd row, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 2 \\ 4 & 2 & -3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 2 \\ 5 & -1 & -2 & 2\end{aligned}| & =0\cdot {C}_{31}+0\cdot {C}_{32}+0\cdot {C}_{33}+2\cdot {C}_{34} \\  & =2\cdot (-1)^{3+4}\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 \\ 4 & 2 & -3 \\ 5 & -1 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =-2\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 \\ 4 & 2 & -3 \\ 5 & -1 & -2\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Expand along row 1, with cofactor signs +, −, +, −. The nonzero entries contribute (-3)(-1)=3 times the minor deleting column 2 and 2 times the minor deleting column 3. This matches option d.

after.name: Question 3
after.worked_solution:
The $1$rst row of the matrix contains two zeros, more than any other row. So using a Laplace expansion along the $1$st row, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}0 & -3 & 2 & 0 \\ 1 & -4 & -3 & 8 \\ 9 & 5 & -3 & -6 \\ -2 & 6 & 7 & 0\end{aligned}| & =0\cdot {C}_{11}+-3\cdot {C}_{12}+2\cdot {C}_{13}+0\cdot {C}_{14} \\  & =-3\cdot (-1)^{1+2}|\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 8 \\ 9 & -3 & -6 \\ -2 & 7 & 0\end{aligned}|+2\cdot (-1)^{1+3}\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 8 \\ 9 & 5 & -6 \\ -2 & 6 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =3\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 8 \\ 9 & -3 & -6 \\ -2 & 7 & 0\end{aligned}|+2\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 8 \\ 9 & 5 & -6 \\ -2 & 6 & 0\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

after.name: Question 4
after.worked_solution:
The $3$rd row of the matrix contains two zeros, more than any other row. So using a Laplace expansion along the $3$rd row, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 3 & 6 & -4 & 1 \\ 0 & -5 & -5 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 5 & 2\end{aligned}| & =0\cdot {C}_{31}+(-5)\cdot {C}_{32}+(-5)\cdot {C}_{33}+0\cdot {C}_{34} \\  & =(-5)\cdot (-1)^{3+2}|\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & -3 \\ 3 & -4 & 1 \\ -1 & 5 & 2\end{aligned}|+(-5)\cdot (-1)^{3+3}\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & -3 \\ 3 & 6 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =5\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & -3 \\ 3 & -4 & 1 \\ -1 & 5 & 2\end{aligned}|-5\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & -3 \\ 3 & 6 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Expand along row 4. The nonzero terms have coefficients (-2)(-1)^{4+2}=-2 and 1(-1)^{4+3}=-1. Deleting row 4 and the corresponding columns gives the two minors in option d.

after.name: Question 5
after.worked_solution:
The $4$th row of the matrix contains two zeros, more than any other row. So using a Laplace expansion along the $4$th row, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & -1 & 0 \\ 1 & 3 & -3 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & -2 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}| & =0\cdot {C}_{41}+(-2)\cdot {C}_{42}+1\cdot {C}_{43}+0\cdot {C}_{44} \\  & =(-2)\cdot (-1)^{4+2}\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 0 \\ 1 & -3 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}|+1\cdot (-1)^{4+3}\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 3 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =-2\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 0 \\ 1 & -3 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}|-|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 3 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Expanding along row 1 gives 3(-1)^{1+3} times the minor with rows (1,2,-1), (0,1,0), (2,-1,3). Expanding that minor along its second row gives 1(3-(-2))=5. Therefore the original determinant is 3·5=15.

after.name: Question 6
after.problem:
Compute the following determinant using a cofactor expansion along the $1$st row:

$$
|\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}|.
$$
after.worked_solution:
Using cofactor expansion along the $1$st row, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}| & =0\cdot {C}_{11}+0\cdot {C}_{12}+3\cdot {C}_{13}+0\cdot {C}_{14} \\  & =3\cdot (-1)^{1+3}\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =3|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, computing the $3\times 3$ determinant by applying a Laplace expansion along the $2$nd row, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}| & =0\cdot {C}_{21}+1\cdot {C}_{22}+0\cdot {C}_{23} \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{2+2}\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =3+2 \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
|\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}|=3\cdot 5=15.

content.knowledge_point: Calculating a Determinant Using a Laplace Expansion Across a Row
content.problem:
Compute the following determinant using a cofactor expansion along the $1$st row:

$$
|\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}|.
$$
content.worked_solution:
Using cofactor expansion along the $1$st row, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}| & =0\cdot {C}_{11}+0\cdot {C}_{12}+3\cdot {C}_{13}+0\cdot {C}_{14} \\  & =3\cdot (-1)^{1+3}\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =3|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, computing the $3\times 3$ determinant by applying a Laplace expansion along the $2$nd row, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}| & =0\cdot {C}_{21}+1\cdot {C}_{22}+0\cdot {C}_{23} \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{2+2}\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =3+2 \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
|\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}|=3\cdot 5=15.
$$

after.worked_solution:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 3 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 4 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}| & =4\cdot {C}_{41}+0\cdot {C}_{42}+0\cdot {C}_{43}+0\cdot {C}_{44} \\  & =4\cdot (-1)^{4+1}\cdot |\begin{aligned}4 & 3 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =-4|\begin{aligned}4 & 3 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}

after.name: Question 8
after.worked_solution:
The $4$th row of the given matrix contains two zeros, more than any other row. So, using a Laplace expansion along the $4$th row, we have   

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ -1 & -1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}| & =2\cdot {C}_{41}+0\cdot {C}_{42}+0\cdot {C}_{43}+3\cdot {C}_{44} \\  & =2\cdot (-1)^{4+1}\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ -1 & 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}|+3\cdot (-1)^{4+4}\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & -2 \\ -1 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-2|\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ -1 & 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}|+3|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & -2 \\ -1 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, computing the first $3\times 3$  determinant by applying a Laplace expansion along the $2$nd row, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ -1 & 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}| & =(-1)\cdot {C}_{21}+2\cdot {C}_{22}+0\cdot {C}_{23} \\  & =(-1)\cdot (-1)^{2+1}\cdot |\begin{aligned}-2 & 3 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|+2\cdot (-1)^{2+2}\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-2 & 3 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|+2|\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-2-3)+2(1-3) \\  & =-5+2\cdot (-2) \\  & =-9\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 11
after.worked_solution:
Using a cofactor expansion along the $4$th column, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}3 & -1 & 4 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & 2 & 5 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 4 & 0\end{aligned}| & =0\cdot {C}_{14}+5\cdot {C}_{24}+0\cdot {C}_{34}+0\cdot {C}_{44} \\  & =5\cdot (-1)^{2+4}\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & -1 & 4 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =5\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & -1 & 4 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

decision.explanation: Expand along column 3. The nonzero entries have cofactor signs (-1)^{1+3}=1 and (-1)^{4+3}=-1, giving √3 times the minor deleting row 1 and column 3, minus √5 times the minor deleting row 4 and column 3. This matches option b.

after.name: Question 13
after.worked_solution:
Using a cofactor expansion along the $3$rd column, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & \sqrt{3} & -1 \\ -1 & -1 & 0 & 1 \\ -2 & 1 & 0 & -1 \\ -1 & 5 & \sqrt{5} & 1\end{aligned}| & =\sqrt{3}\cdot {C}_{13}+0\cdot {C}_{23}+0\cdot {C}_{33}+\sqrt{5}\cdot {C}_{43} \\  & =\sqrt{3}\cdot (-1)^{1+3}\cdot |\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 & 1 \\ -2 & 1 & -1 \\ -1 & 5 & 1\end{aligned}|+\sqrt{5}\cdot (-1)^{4+3}\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & -1 \\ -1 & -1 & 1 \\ -2 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =\sqrt{3}\cdot |\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 & 1 \\ -2 & 1 & -1 \\ -1 & 5 & 1\end{aligned}|-\sqrt{5}\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & -1 \\ -1 & -1 & 1 \\ -2 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

content.worked_solution:
Using a cofactor expansion along the $3$rd column, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & \sqrt{3} & -1 \\ -1 & -1 & 0 & 1 \\ -2 & 1 & 0 & -1 \\ -1 & 5 & \sqrt{5} & 1\end{aligned}| & =\sqrt{3}\cdot {C}_{13}+0\cdot {C}_{23}+0\cdot {C}_{33}+\sqrt{5}\cdot {C}_{43} \\  & =\sqrt{3}\cdot (-1)^{1+3}\cdot |\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 & 1 \\ -2 & 1 & -1 \\ -1 & 5 & 1\end{aligned}|+\sqrt{5}\cdot (-1)^{4+3}\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & -1 \\ -1 & -1 & 1 \\ -2 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =\sqrt{3}\cdot |\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 & 1 \\ -2 & 1 & -1 \\ -1 & 5 & 1\end{aligned}|-\sqrt{5}\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & -1 \\ -1 & -1 & 1 \\ -2 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Expand along column 2. Its only nonzero entry is 2 in row 3, with cofactor sign (-1)^{3+2}=-1. Thus the determinant is -2 times the minor formed by deleting row 3 and column 2, matching option c.

after.name: Question 14
after.worked_solution:
Using a cofactor expansion along the $2$nd column, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 & 1 & 5 \\ -4 & 0 & -3 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & -4 & 3 \\ -1 & 0 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}| & =0\cdot {C}_{12}+0\cdot {C}_{22}+2\cdot {C}_{32}+0\cdot {C}_{42} \\  & =2\cdot (-1)^{3+2}\cdot |\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & 5 \\ -4 & -3 & 2 \\ -1 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =-2\cdot |\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & 5 \\ -4 & -3 & 2 \\ -1 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Using a cofactor expansion along the $2$nd column, we have

$$

after.worked_solution:
Using a cofactor expansion along the $2$nd column, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -4 & 3 \\ -1 & -7 & 5 & -1 \\ 2 & 0 & 6 & -2 \\ -2 & -8 & -9 & 4\end{aligned}| & =0\cdot {C}_{12}+(-7)\cdot {C}_{22}+0\cdot {C}_{32}+(-8)\cdot {C}_{42} \\  & =(-7)\cdot (-1)^{2+2}|\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 3 \\ 2 & 6 & -2 \\ -2 & -9 & 4\end{aligned}|+(-8)\cdot (-1)^{4+2}\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 3 \\ -1 & 5 & -1 \\ 2 & 6 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =-7\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 3 \\ 2 & 6 & -2 \\ -2 & -9 & 4\end{aligned}|-8\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 3 \\ -1 & 5 & -1 \\ 2 & 6 & -2\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

content.worked_solution:
Using a cofactor expansion along the $2$nd column, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -4 & 3 \\ -1 & -7 & 5 & -1 \\ 2 & 0 & 6 & -2 \\ -2 & -8 & -9 & 4\end{aligned}| & =0\cdot {C}_{12}+(-7)\cdot {C}_{22}+0\cdot {C}_{32}+(-8)\cdot {C}_{42} \\  & =(-7)\cdot (-1)^{2+2}|\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 3 \\ 2 & 6 & -2 \\ -2 & -9 & 4\end{aligned}|+(-8)\cdot (-1)^{4+2}\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 3 \\ -1 & 5 & -1 \\ 2 & 6 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =-7\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 3 \\ 2 & 6 & -2 \\ -2 & -9 & 4\end{aligned}|-8\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 3 \\ -1 & 5 & -1 \\ 2 & 6 & -2\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$
